question: Who invented paper?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cai Lun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cai Lun** was a Chinese eunuch and political official who is widely regarded as the inventor of paper.
 
• He lived during the Eastern Han Dynasty in China, around 50-121 AD.
 
• Cai Lun's invention involved using mulberry bark, hemp, rags, and fishnets, which was a significant improvement over earlier writing materials such as bamboo and silk.
 
• His method of papermaking was quickly adopted and spread throughout China and eventually the world, revolutionizing the way information was recorded and disseminated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baudhayan**

 
 
• Baudhayan was an ancient Indian mathematician and priest who is best known for his work in geometry and mathematics.
 
• He authored the Baudhāyana Śulbasûtra, which contains some of the earliest known statements of the Pythagorean theorem and the value of π (pi).
 
• Baudhayan's work laid the foundation for later developments in Indian mathematics and influenced future mathematicians such as Aryabhata and Brahmagupta.
 
 
 
• **Mahaviracharya**
 
 
• Mahaviracharya was an Indian mathematician who lived in the 9th century AD.
 
• He is best known for his work "Ganita Sara Samgraha", which is a comprehensive treatise on mathematics covering topics such as arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and combinatorics.
 
• Mahaviracharya's contributions to mathematics include the concept of zero, operations on fractions, and the rules for solving quadratic equations.
 
 
 
• **Varahamihira**
 
 
• Varahamihira was an Indian astronomer, mathematician, and astrologer who lived during the 6th century AD.
 
• He is best known for his work "Brihat Samhita", which is an encyclopedic treatise on various subjects including astronomy, astrology, geography, architecture, and weather prediction.
 
• Varahamihira made significant contributions to the field of astronomy, including the discovery of the concept of reflection and refraction of light.
